content_preview.title: VS Code 1.128 Ships Multi-Chat Agent Sessions and GA Copilot Vision
content_preview.summary: Visual Studio Code 1.128 lets a single Claude agent-host session hold multiple parallel chats and moves Copilot Vision to general availability.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft released [Visual Studio Code 1.128](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_128) on July 8, 2026, adding the ability to run several related chats inside a single Claude agent-host session, moving Copilot Vision's image and PDF support to general availability, and letting extensions register keyboard shortcuts that fire even when the editor isn't in focus.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis). 620 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Prose is neutral, technically precise, and each paragraph is anchored to a specific cited claim rather than generic filler.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and snapshot sha256 hashes were independently recomputed from the gzip files and match the manifest exactly (source-0.html.gz=103824f5..., source-1.html.gz=d1f5e087..., source-2.html.gz=6feebbeb...). I extracted and read the full text of all three snapshots. source-0.html.gz (code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_128): confirms release date July 8, 2026, and every direct quote attributed to it appears verbatim in the snapshot, including 'provide agentic coding capabilities powered by Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK directly in VS Code,' 'compare approaches, branch from an earlier turn, and run work in parallel,' 'For questions not tied to a folder, you can now start a chat in the Agents window without selecting a workspace,' 'their transcripts appear as read-only peer chats,' 'Multimodal support is now generally available in VS Code, starting with this latest release,' 'by pasting them into Chat, dragging and dropping them, or using the context menu,' 'these shortcuts take effect even if VS Code is not in focus,' and 'organizations can mandate where GitHub Copilot sends OpenTelemetry (OTel) data, so that telemetry flows to an approved collector.' The workbench.browser.newTabPlacement description and the BYOK/sampling-parameters summary are accurate paraphrases of the source's Editor Experience/Chat sections. source-1.html.gz (github.blog changelog): confirms 'Agentic browser tools are now generally available' and the 'Use multiple chats in one session' entry under Parallel sessions and chats, supporting the article's framing that 1.128 continues a broader June-July release cycle; note the changelog itself explicitly says it covers v1.123-v1.127 (not v1.128 by version number), but the article's phrasing ('situates 1.128 within a broader release cycle') is careful not to claim the changelog discusses 1.128 directly, and the framing is accurate. source-2.html.gz (nTCompatible): independently confirms the July 8, 2026 release date, byline Philipp Esselbach, and the 'AI-native development environment' characterization is drawn near-verbatim from the source's own words ('an always-on, AI-native development environment' / 'positions VS Code as one of the first mainstream IDEs with native support for Claude's agentic behavior'). No misattribution, no hallucinated quotes, and the outlet cited matches the content fetched.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific in the article (release version 1.128, release date July 8 2026, feature names, setting names such as workbench.browser.newTabPlacement and chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled, and the internal cross-reference to the prior VS Code 1.123 article) traces to a cited source. The internal link to /article/2026-06/09-vs-code-1123-... resolves to an existing published article and its described feature (cross-machine agent session syncing / 'Session sync and chronicle') is corroborated by the GitHub changelog snapshot. No fabricated specifics found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no sensationalism or editorializing. The Analysis section offers interpretive framing clearly separated from the factual reporting in What We Know.
editor_notes.originality: New topic, not covered by any existing article. Checked src/content/articles/2026-07/ for duplicate VS Code/Copilot coverage; the only prior related piece is the June 2026 VS Code 1.123 article, which this submission correctly cites as prior coverage of a related but distinct feature (session sync vs. multi-chat sessions).
editor_notes.false_positive_note: The automated script flagged 'Contains AI self-reference' via the regex /\bas an ai\b/i. I traced the match: it hits the substring 'as an AI' inside '...position VS Code as an AI-native development environment...' in the closing paragraph of 'What We Know.' This is a product-positioning description (also used near-verbatim by the nTCompatible source itself), not first-person AI self-reference (e.g. 'As an AI, I...') that the editorial policy's no-self-reference rule is meant to catch. Since there is no actual factual error, fabrication, or misattribution to disclose to readers, writing a corrections record here would be dishonest — there is nothing to correct. I am overriding the automated APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS suggestion to APPROVE on this basis, per my Chief Editor authority to make the final verdict (Step 6). The findings array is left untouched per process, as it accurately reflects the raw pattern match; this note documents why I judged it non-actionable.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced, accurately quoted News submission. The single automated warning is a mechanical regex false positive, verified by manual inspection of context, and does not warrant a corrections record. APPROVE.
